classification.difficultyReason: Read whether graph branches join at a specified point, distinguishing open and closed endpoints.

content.prompt: State whether each function is continuous at the given point.

spec.description: Black schematic graph with a closed endpoint at (2,0), an open endpoint at (2,3), and dashed guides.
spec.mathematics: The left branch reaches (2,0); the right branch approaches (2,3). The graph has a jump at x=2. Curves are schematic because no equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and givens are always visible; continuity judgement is answer-only.

answer.worked: Discontinuous at $x=2$: the left branch ends at $(2,0)$, while the right branch approaches the open point $(2,3)$. The branches do not join.

spec.description: A smooth increasing curve through (0,1) joins a horizontal right ray at (2,3); dashed guides mark the joining point.
spec.mathematics: The curved and horizontal branches meet at (2,3) with no hole or jump. No equation is specified.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and givens are always visible; continuity judgement is answer-only.

answer.worked: Continuous at $x=2$: the curve joins the horizontal branch at $(2,3)$ without a break.

spec.description: A rising left ray ends at the filled point (0,2). A separate decreasing curve to the right passes through (2,2) and (3,0), descending towards the vertical dashed line x=4.
spec.mathematics: The value at x=0 is 2, but the right-hand curve does not join that point. Dashed guides identify (2,2); x=4 is a vertical dashed guide. No formula is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and givens are always visible; continuity judgement is answer-only.

answer.worked: Discontinuous at $x=0$: $f(0)=2$, but the curve to the right does not join the filled point $(0,2)$.

spec.description: A horizontal left ray ends at the filled point (0,2). A rising segment runs from the open origin to (2,2), joining a horizontal right ray. Dashed guides mark (2,2).
spec.mathematics: At the requested point x=2 the rising and horizontal pieces meet at y=2. The separate endpoint convention at x=0 is preserved.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and givens are always visible; continuity judgement is answer-only.

answer.worked: Continuous at $x=2$: the rising segment and horizontal branch meet at $(2,2)$ without a break.
